answer_text:
Yes.

Suppose, for contradiction, that \(u \neq 0\). Define a linear functional on the one-dimensional subspace \(\mathbb{F}u \subseteq X\) by

\[
g(\alpha u)=\alpha \|u\|_X,
\]

where \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R}\) or \(\mathbb{C}\). Then

\[
\|g\|_{(\mathbb{F}u)^*}
=
\sup_{\alpha \neq 0}\frac{|g(\alpha u)|}{\|\alpha u\|_X}
=
\sup_{\alpha \neq 0}\frac{|\alpha|\|u\|_X}{|\alpha|\|u\|_X}
=1.
\]

By the Hahn–Banach theorem, \(g\) extends to a continuous linear functional \(f \in X^*\) such that \(\|f\|_{X^*}=1\). In particular,

\[
\langle f,u\rangle_{X^*\times X}=f(u)=\|u\|_X \neq 0.
\]

This contradicts the assumption that \(\langle f,u\rangle=0\) for every \(f\in X^*\). Therefore the assumption \(u\neq 0\) is false, so \(u=0\), and hence \(\|u\|_X=0\).

\[
\boxed{\text{Yes, necessarily } \|u\|_X=0.}
\]
